For any positive amount funded on the contract, a withdraw() call by the Owner succeeds and empties the contract, i.e. address(c).balance == 0 afterwards; the mutant drops the transfer, leaving a nonzero balance.

For any owner-called withdraw, the entire contract balance is transferred out to the owner and the contract balance drops to zero; the mutant sending to msg.sender instead of Owner is observable when the caller/owner distinction matters.

For any fuzzed amount, a successful withdraw() by the owner must drain the entire contract balance out of c (address(c).balance becomes 0); the mutant breaks the recipient convention so a caller-funded path can leave balance discrepancies, which the fuzzer can expose.

For any admissible funded amount, a successful withdraw() by the owner must transfer the entire contract balance out of c, leaving address(c).balance == 0 and crediting exactly that balance to the owner; the mutant violates the recipient convention so it cannot be relied on to pay the owner the drained balance.

For any admissible caller and amount, a successful withdraw() must pay the entire contract balance to the account at c.Owner() (leaving address(c).balance == 0 and crediting the owner exactly the drained amount), and any caller other than the owner must revert without moving funds — the mutant pays the caller instead of the owner, violating the recipient convention whenever caller and owner differ.

For any admissible input, a successful owner withdraw() drains the entire contract balance and credits exactly that amount to the account stored in c.Owner(); the mutant credits the caller instead of the owner, breaking the recipient convention whenever caller and owner differ.
Only the owner may successfully withdraw: a withdraw call from a non-owner must revert (P reverts, M succeeds).
